text: The Patriots are heading to Buffalo for a crucial Week 4 AFC East matchup against the 3-0 Bills as a 1-2 team, and the week has brought both reinforcement and setback along the offensive line: the team signed OL Matt Pryor from the Arizona Cardinals practice squad to shore up the unit, but placed guard Greg Van Roten on injured reserve due to a thigh injury, continuing a frustrating string of challenges around quarterback Drake Maye. Speaking Wednesday, Maye insisted his right shoulder is fine and emphasized that his early-season struggles stem not from physical limitations but from poor decision-making, a self-assessment that rings particularly true given New England's offensive dysfunction—the unit currently ranks dead last in the NFL at just 9.7 points per game. The Patriots will face a Bills team riding a three-game winning streak and led by Josh Allen, whose history suggests he can quickly move past sloppy performances, making New England's need for offensive efficiency all the more urgent. Off the field, Ann Michael Maye, the quarterback's wife, made a $100,000 donation through the MayeDay Family Foundation to Family Food Connections on Tuesday while volunteering to distribute groceries to families facing food insecurity.
